items.difficulty_reason: For continuous homomorphisms from a ring A to rings B and C, the lemma asserts that if the map from A to B is taut then so is the map from C to the completed tensor product of B and C over A (statement lines 1387-1392). The proof fixes an open ideal of C, chooses an open ideal of A whose image lies in it, and uses tautness of the given map to identify the completed tensor product as the limit of the tensor products of the quotients, which says exactly that the ideals generated by the two chosen ideals form a fundamental system of open ideals of the completed tensor product (proof lines 1394-1401). It then observes that the closure of the ideal generated by the chosen ideal of C in the completed tensor product equals the sum of that ideal and the ideal generated by the chosen ideal of A, because continuity of the canonical map from B forces the latter ideal inside that closure; this is exactly the condition of tautness for the map from C (proof lines 1401-1407). The claim is H2: the argument identifies a fundamental system of open ideals and then computes one closure, and both steps are displayed; it is short but not a citation.
